title: Asking for a position that isn't there
idea: If you index past the end of a list, Python raises an error. Learn which indexes are safe and which go too far — without using len() yet.

exercises.prompt: A list has 3 values: nums = [3, 7, 2]. What are the valid positive indexes?
exercises.explanation: Three values fill positions 0, 1, 2. There is no position 3 — the count starts at 0, so the last index is one less than the number of values.

exercises.prompt: nums = [3, 7, 2] has three values. What happens with  print(nums[3])?
options: An error — there is no value at index 3
exercises.explanation: The valid indexes are 0, 1, 2. Index 3 is past the end, so Python raises an 'index out of range' error.

exercises.prompt: For a list of 4 values, index 4 is one step too far.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Four values fill 0, 1, 2, 3. Index 4 does not exist, so asking for it is an error. The last valid index is one less than the count.

exercises.prompt: nums = [10, 20] has two values. Which index is SAFE?
exercises.explanation: Two values live at 0 and 1. nums[1] is 20, which is fine. Anything from 2 upward is out of range.

exercises.prompt: For nums = [5, 6, 7] (three values), match each index to safe or error.
exercises.explanation: Valid indexes are 0, 1, 2. Index 3 goes past the end of a three-value list and causes an error.

exercises.prompt: Why is asking for a position past the end an ERROR, not just an empty answer?
options: There is genuinely no value there, so Python stops and tells you
Python is being strict for no reason
The list secretly has more values
exercises.explanation: An out-of-range index points at nothing real. Rather than guess, Python stops and reports the mistake clearly so you can fix it.

exercises.prompt: An EMPTY list is empty = []. What happens with  print(empty[0])?
options: An error — there is no value at index 0
exercises.explanation: An empty list has no values at all, so even index 0 points at nothing. Indexing it is an out-of-range error.

exercises.prompt: The largest valid index of a list is one less than the number of values.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Five values fill 0 to 4; the biggest index is 4, one less than 5. That is the direct result of starting at 0.

exercises.prompt: nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. Which line would cause an out-of-range ERROR?
exercises.explanation: Five values fill 0 to 4, so nums[5] is past the end. nums[4] is the last valid one (value 5), and -1 safely means the last value too.

exercises.prompt: You want the third value of nums = [8, 9] but there are only two values. What should you expect?
options: An error — there is no third value to get
It returns the second value instead
It adds a third value for you
exercises.explanation: The list only has positions 0 and 1. Asking for index 2 (the third value) is out of range, so Python raises an error.
